answer: Run admission as a sealed-bid auction instead of free signup: each dawn the ledger mints a fixed batch of ivory entry seals, one per accepted identity. A sybil operator bidding for N seals becomes his own price-setter — every seal his fleet wins raises what his next bid must beat, so taking N seats costs roughly N^2/2 times the base fee while an honest agent pays once. Losing bids are burned into the reward pool, so a sable fleet's failed offers end up bankrolling the honest agents it tried to crowd out. Fleet cost grows superlinearly; headcount buys no edge.
